body: Now it is difficult to imagine that once 200 years ago there was no lake here - it looks so organic here. The lake is the last visible act of the last king of Kandy with the hard-to-pronounce name Sri Vikram Rajasingh as always in Ceylon. The lake was dug up in 1807, apparently primarily to solve the problem of water supply, although there is an erotic legend that the King's concubines bathed on an island in the centre of the lake. However, another theory says they also bathed in the pavilion on the shores of the Ulpange, which unlike the island is accessible. Either the king had so many concubines that they could not fit on the island and bathed on the shores, or there was an exaggeration somewhere. After the conquest of Ceylon, the erotically restrained inhabitants of the foggy Albion chose to use the island not for bodily comfort, but to place an arsenal there to store ammunition. Herons, pelicans and cormorants now use the island. A second legend related to the island states that after the treason of the first minister of the aforementioned king, he defected to the English. The king ordered the beheading of all his children, after which the distraught mother threw herself into the lake waters and drowned herself. And you can kind of still hear the suicidal man moaning and crying. It's a mix of the Greek myth of Niob, Wilde's "The Canterville Ghost" and Conan-Doyle's "The Dogs of Baskerville." You can walk along the lake, but you can't drink from it for half a century. You can be a goat...
title: The legends of Lake Kandy...

body: An absolutely breathtaking lake that beautifully complements the charm, serenity, and cultural richness of Kandy. Surrounded by lush greenery, ancient temples, and colonial-era architecture, Kandy Lake is a peaceful retreat right in the heart of the bustling city. It offers a calm and picturesque setting, ideal for those who wish to enjoy a quiet evening stroll, take in the scenic views, or simply reflect in nature’s stillness.One of the best places to experience its full beauty is from the Kandy Lake Viewpoint, also known as Arthur’s Seat. This elevated spot, nestled along Rajapihilla Mawatha, provides sweeping panoramic views of the sacred Kandy Lake (Kiri Muhuda), the Temple of the Tooth Relic (Sri Dalada Maligawa), and the city’s rolling hills beyond. The lake itself was constructed in 1807 by King Sri Wickrama Rajasinghe, the last monarch of the Kandyan Kingdom, as part of a grand vision to enhance the city’s spiritual and royal prestige.Today, it remains not only a historical landmark but also a favorite among both locals and tourists seeking peace, beauty, and a deep connection to Kandy’s royal past. Whether you're a photographer, a nature lover, a spiritual seeker, or simply exploring Sri Lanka, this spot is a must-visit for anyone wanting to witness the timeless elegance and tranquility of Kandy.
title: An absolutely breathtaking lake view in Kandy.!

We also saw lots of beautifully coloured birds such as kingfishers and also terrapins, small lizards, butterflies, pelicans and lots of fish. body: I was in Kandy for 4 days. Stayed in a hostel near the train station and Kandy Lake is about half an hour walk from the train station. The Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic is located at the southern end of the lake. The grand Victorian architectural style colonial Queens Hotel stands robustly opposite the lake. Kandy Lake reminded me of Hoan Kiem Lake in Hanoi. It was winter when I visited Hanoi few years back and I enjoyed my stroll around the lake in the comfortably cold weather. When exhaustion set in, I would just relax on the bench at the lakeside admiring the tranquility of the atmosphere. But the experience at Kandy Lake was different. The weather was terribly hot and humid in the month of March and the air was still. There were not many benches available and most were fully occupied by the locals. The incessant traffic flow at the northern end of the lake flooded my lungs with much toxic pollutants. It was not a place where you can really appreciate the lake scenery. The stretch of the lake near to the temple was much more peaceful as only few vehicles ply this road. While strolling along this stretch of the lake, I was surprised to find a gigantic monitor lizard crawling at one side of the lake. This is my first time seeing such a gigantic lizard emerging out of the water. At another corner, oblivious to the curious eyes of the onlookers, few beautiful geese with brightly colored feathers were seen mating and having fun in the water. The long slim legged white cranes hunt for her prey beneath the water surface. It was a fun filled nature world for the birds and animals as they wandered freely in their natural instinct at the lake side. As I passed the Temple of the Tooth Relics, I could see flock of devotees carrying bouquet of flowers in their hands climbing up the stairs into the temple halls. As dusk slowly crept in, the lake view became dim while the neon lights in the temple shone brilliantly out and brighten one end of the lake. This was Buddha's Lake of compassion. The fishes, the monitor lizards, the cranes, the geese and whatever form of lives on top or beneath the lake are well protected in this land of the Buddha. That makes Kandy Lake different from West Lake, Sun Moon Lake, Hoan Kiem Lake, Houhai, Xihai and the rest of the lakes. As I walked my way to my hostel, the quotes of Buddha resonates in my mind:'Besides the respect of the lives of human beings, all the animals and plants should be on the list too. That is the real humanitarianism.'
title: Buddha's Lake of compassion

body: For my health I have to walk a couple of miles a day, and while the perimeter of Kandy Lake is actually a couple fo kilometers, it meets my needs nicely. The walkway around the lake is under construction and there are many patches where you need to go into the street, but the water is lovely, so are the ducks and the schools of fish that congregate in certain spots waiting to be fed by passersby. At the farther end (from City Center) there are numerous vendors of snacks, drinks and ice cream to counteract the effects of the exercise you get by walking. Only once criticism is that there aren't enough benches along the shore. Those that do exist are always full, and it would be nice to be able to take a break during the walk, though it is not strenuous at all. I'm only giving this a 4 because of the construction. There is of course a lot of car exhaust as it is in the middle of the city, but on the other hand also a lot of shade trees that cool things down along with constant lake breezes.

body: Kandy is a busy city, and regardless of which direction you come in from you'll find a bit chaotic compared to wherever you spent the previous night! The lake is a slight distraction from that (but only slight, as there's a busy road alongside half of it!) The walk around is not long, and right now is slightly challenging as they seem to be replacing most of the footpaths on north side if the lake, but get past that and take your time and you might get the opportunity to see a bit of wildlife. We meandered round and saw plenty of birdlife - including a kingfisher catching fish and insects - plus aquatic monitor lizards, a few turtles, and the ubiquitous fish that inhabit the lake. OK, it's an artificial lake, and the bustling traffic kill the peacefulness around the south of the lake, but it's free and if you take your time and keep your eyes open it can be a nice distraction from the madness of the city.

body: Kandy lake or kiri-muhuda is situated opposite temple of the tooth in Kandy. This area was earlier a Paddy field later converted to a lake by king Sri Wikrama rajasinghe the last king of Kandy in early 1800's. The wall surrounding the lake is known as the "walakulu bamma" or the cloud wall. The royal architect Devendra Moolacharya has designed the lake and wall in a way where if someone go to the opposite side of the lake to appear the temple as it is floating in the sky. Another attraction is the queens bath situated close to the temple and the island at the middle of the lake where it was a resting place for king.
title: Kirimuhuda once was a ancient Paddy field

Now, vehicles have to travel around the Kandy Lake because the road running past the Temple of the Tooth was closed after a bomb exploded outside many years ago. The lake was built by the last King of the Kandyan Kingdom around 1807 before the British deviously conquered the kingdom and brought the whole island under colonial rule. You wouldn't want to walk around the lake now, unless you want to inhale the pollution generated by the continuous stream of vehicles chugging around it. It's a real shame!

body: Kandy Lake is a dominating part of Kandy city, and you can`t miss it! The lake is charming and peaceful and is our absolute favorite part of Kandy.The lake was created in 1807 by the last ruler of the kingdom of Kandy. The people initially objected to laboring on the lake project, but those who objected were ruthlessly put to death on stakes in the lake bed. So the lake has a bloody history.In the middle of the lake is a small island used by the emperor`s personal harem. Later the British used it to store ammunition, and they were the ones who built the fortress style parapet around the area.

body: The Kandy Lake offers a wonderful place for a stroll or a jog. The shady path surrounding the lake provides a view of the hills and the town. The spectacular lake was created in 1807 by the last Sinhalese King. It is situated by the side of the Temple of the tooth relic. The Malwatte temple, one of the two head temples of the Siyam Nikaya sect of Theravada Buddhism, is also located overlooking the lake. Sri Wickrama Rajasinghe, the last king of Kandy, decorated the lake with the "walakulu" (clouds) wall.

title: Experience the essence of beauty with a little bit of history.
body: Kandy is essentially the gateway to the hill country of Sri Lanka. Scenic towns like Nuwara Eliya, Badulla, Bandarawela, Ella and the famous Horton Plains are all reached via Kandy. This city is the second largest city in Sri lanka. I personally prefer to call it a town rather than a city, Kandy is a go-to destination in any sri Lankan travel itinerary. Established somewhere around mid 1400's, kandy was the last seat of the Sri Lankan Kings. Set in the heart of the Kandy town is the Kandy Lake. Take a walk around the lake in the evenings at dusk. It is probably the best time to enjoy the lake, and the town, which otherwise seems to be a mad crowd of vehicles. The lake walk is elevated above the road level so you are above the clutter.The famous Temple of the Tooth Relic or the Dalada Maligawa is on North Bank of theLake. As you walk down the Norther walkway along the Temple of the Tooth Relic, you come to a small gem of a pavilion on the right side, set partly on the lake itself. This is the little know Queens bathing Pavilion.. The royal ladies of the Kandyan court used this pavilion when bathing in the lake. Originally a single storey structure, the upper level was added by the british and the building later used as a library. More recently used as a police post, this little gem is currently under restoration. The Queens hotel is just across the road on the west of the lake. There are a few hotels along the south bank but non that offer a worthy view or experience that i would recommend.
